recent_posts.title: Announcing the Second-Ever CCC Community Chat, “A New Era of Scientific Progress: Uniting Advanced Computing and Citizen Science for Accelerated Research” » CCC Blog
recent_posts.summary: The Computing Community Consortium (CCC) is hosting a webinar on May 20, 2026, exploring the convergence of citizen science and advanced computing research. Authors of the CCC Grand Challenges report will discuss how AI and other technologies can augment citizen science projects, address national priorities, and what infrastructure changes are needed for large-scale convergence. Guest speaker Marc Kuchner (NASA Citizen Science Officer) and Tanya Berger-Wolf (Ohio State University) will give lightning talks, followed by a live Q&A with the report's lead authors.

recent_posts.title: Assessing Security Considerations for Artificial Intelligence
recent_posts.summary: The U.S. Center for AI Standards and Innovation (CAISI/NIST) issued a Request for Information on securing AI agent systems, and the Computing Community Consortium (CCC) and Computing Research Association (CRA) submitted a joint response. Key challenges identified include delegating credentials to AI agents, determining accountability for security failures, and preventing cascade effects in multi-agent systems. Recommendations include reevaluating fuzz testing and input sanitization for autonomous agents, researching effective guardrails, assessing multi-agent risks, and shifting toward security-by-design rather than post-deployment patching. The response also emphasizes the importance of human-in-the-loop practices and stronger collaboration between research communities and industry cybersecurity practitioners.

recent_posts.title: Ensuring American Scientific Leadership through the Convergence of Computing and Citizen Science
recent_posts.summary: A Computing Community Consortium (CCC) workshop report outlines grand challenges and strategic recommendations for converging advanced computing and citizen science. The report argues this convergence can enhance national competitiveness, improve government efficiency, develop STEM workforce skills, and address pressing challenges like natural disaster response. Key infrastructure recommendations include cross-agency collaboration, permanent federal funding streams, interoperable AI-ready data standards (FAIR data), privacy-preserving frameworks (federated learning, data trusts), explainable AI governance, and a proposed National Citizen Science & AI Convergence Hub.

recent_posts.title: What Does It Take to Be an Effective Leader and Mentor in Research Supporting At-Risk Technology Users? » CCC Blog
recent_posts.summary: The Computing Community Consortium (CCC) has published a brief on leading and mentoring in research that supports at-risk technology users (SARU). The brief covers three main areas: fostering rigorous research skills in team members through low-stakes learning environments, crafting proactive support plans that address researcher wellbeing, work-life boundaries, and risks like harassment or doxxing, and building community through cross-disciplinary collaboration, workshops, and asynchronous groups. The goal is to equip senior researchers with guidance to support early-career researchers in this sensitive and potentially harmful field.

recent_posts.title: Call for Papers: CCC-Sponsored Blue Sky Track at ICDM 2026 » CCC Blog
recent_posts.summary: The Computing Community Consortium (CCC) is sponsoring the Blue Sky Ideas track at ICDM 2026 (IEEE International Conference on Data Mining), held November 12-15, 2026 in Shenyang, China. The track invites visionary research papers that propose bold, forward-looking ideas, expose gaps in current data mining research, or challenge prevailing assumptions. Submissions are limited to 4 pages in IEEE format and are due July 1, 2026. Accepted papers appear in conference workshop proceedings, and top submissions receive CCC-sponsored travel grants of $500–$1,000.

recent_posts.title: CCC report on converging AI and citizen science for broader research impact
recent_posts.summary: The Computing Community Consortium (CCC) has published a report outlining how advanced computing and AI can amplify citizen science efforts. The report identifies a symbiotic relationship where AI handles large-scale data processing while citizen scientists provide contextual knowledge and edge-case observations. It proposes a research roadmap covering human-AI teaming frameworks, explainable AI for non-expert users, real-time feedback systems, participatory AI governance, and cross-disciplinary collaboration. Key application areas include endangered species protection, medical research acceleration, and astrophysics. The report also emphasizes building ML/AI literacy among both researchers and the general public to enable a new generation of convergence-ready contributors.

recent_posts.title: Call for Papers: CCC-Sponsored Blue Sky Track at ACM ICMI 2026 » CCC Blog
recent_posts.summary: The Computing Community Consortium (CCC) is sponsoring a Blue Sky Ideas Track at ACM ICMI 2026, the 28th International Conference on Multimodal Interaction, held in Napoli, Italy (October 5-9, 2026). The track invites visionary, high-risk research papers at the intersection of multimodal AI and social interaction, with this year's theme being 'Context and Cultural Awareness for Multimodal Interaction.' Submissions are limited to 4 pages, due May 8, 2026. CCC will award travel grants of $1,000, $750, and $500 to the top three papers. ACM's new Open Access policy applies, with subsidized APCs available for 2026.

recent_posts.title: Navigating and Increasing the Use of AI in Clinical Care
recent_posts.summary: The Computing Community Consortium (CCC) and Computing Research Association – Industry (CRA-I) submitted a response to an HHS request for information on advancing AI in clinical care. Key themes include addressing public hesitancy around AI reliability and HIPAA-compliant data security, the potential for AI to reduce clinician burnout through documentation assistance and decision support, and recommendations such as consulting healthcare professionals, keeping models updated with local data, avoiding fully autonomous models, and creating safety evaluation frameworks. The response also highlights a growing urban-rural 'AI gap' and recommends three research priorities: AI-driven clinical decision support, human-AI collaboration, and evaluation frameworks for AI deployment trajectories.

recent_posts.title: Recap: “Beyond Code” Visioning Workshop on AI and Software Systems
recent_posts.summary: The Computing Community Consortium (CCC) and IEEE Computer Society co-hosted the 'Beyond Code: Engineering Trustworthy Software Systems with AI at Scale' workshop in San Francisco on February 25-26, 2026. Dozens of experts from academia, industry, government, and NGOs gathered to discuss AI's current impact and chart a responsible roadmap for using AI to build complex, interdependent software systems. Key topics included the evolving role of computer scientists, AI education, human-AI collaboration, AI output trustworthiness, and accountability. A full workshop report synthesizing findings and research/policy recommendations is expected in 2027. The CCC also launched an AI Research Ecosystem discussion forum inviting broader community input.

recent_posts.title: Enhancing Scientific Capability by Converging AI and Citizen Science
recent_posts.summary: The Computing Community Consortium (CCC) has published a workshop report outlining grand challenges for converging AI and citizen science. Drawing on input from 46 experts across academia, NGOs, industry, and federal agencies, the report identifies five strategic priorities: creating novel human-AI interaction models, improving feedback loops between volunteers and scientists, building trustworthy systems, ensuring data security and privacy, and designing scalable infrastructure. Key recommendations include establishing a national convergence infrastructure, advancing foundational socio-technical research, and developing human capital. The report argues that volunteer citizen scientists provide data labeling, analysis, and creativity that complements AI capabilities, and that combining both can accelerate scientific discovery across ecological, clinical, and infrastructural domains.
